facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Novelis Inc. enters the latest quarter with higher leverage than a year earlier and thinner liquidity, while earnings are improving. Company-defined net leverage was 2.9x at March 31, 2025, 4.1x at March 31, 2026 and 4.7x at September 30, 2026 (RQ4 page:10; RQ2 page:10). The rise comes from the numerator: total debt principal grew from 6,212 at March 31, 2025 to 7,978 at March 31, 2026 and 9,797 at September 30, 2026 (AR page:145; Q2R page:17), while cash was 1,036, 1,254 and 1,277 at the same dates and trailing Adjusted EBITDA moved from 1,802 to 1,645 to 1,831. Cash used in operations was negative 418 in the six months ended September 30, 2026 against positive 411 a year earlier, and capital expenditure was 1,543 against 913 (Q2R page:4 to page:5), so the Bay Minette plant and the Oswego fires absorbed more cash than operations produced. The funding came from the asset-based revolver, which carried about 2.3 billion of borrowings at September 30, 2026 against 935 at March 31, 2026 (Q2R page:18 to page:19; AR page:146), a 500 term loan taken in July 2026 (Q2R page:21) and 950 of equity contributions from the parent in fiscal 2026 (AR page:111). Liquidity of 2,038 is 718 below the 2,756 at March 31, 2026; availability under committed facilities fell to 761 from 1,502 while cash rose to 1,277 from 1,254, and the filing attributes the decrease primarily to a higher revolver balance (Q2R page:61 to page:62). The latest quarter itself was strong on a reported basis: Adjusted EBITDA of 508 against 422 and net income of 210 against 163 (RQ2 page:9; Q2R page:3), but part of the Adjusted EBITDA gain is a 39 business interruption recovery and favorable metal and scrap effects that management itself cites (RQ2 page:2). Management expects capital spending to fall as Bay Minette moves to start-up and forecasts positive free cash flow and a start of deleveraging toward the end of fiscal 2027 (RQ2 page:3); that is a management expectation and is not used in any figure here.

facts.label: Definition review
facts.text: - Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure. The reconciliation adds back or removes: metal price lag (a deduction of 515 in fiscal 2026 and of 257 in the six months ended September 30, 2026), Oswego fire losses net of recoveries (925 and 236), restructuring and impairment (195 and 24), start-up costs (38 and 44) and a proportional consolidation adjustment for the Logan joint venture (55 in fiscal 2026) (RQ4 page:9; RQ2 page:9; AR page:187). The fire add-back was negative 29 in the quarter, because recoveries exceeded charges. - Start-up costs are excluded now, and the company states it "will cease excluding such start-up costs from its Adjusted EBITDA once normal production capacity is achieved at the Bay Minette plant" (Q2R page:68). All else equal, Adjusted EBITDA will then be lower than on the present definition; this is an inference from the stated change, not a company figure. - Business interruption insurance recoveries of 39 are cited by management as a driver of the quarter's Adjusted EBITDA improvement (RQ2 page:2). Cumulative insurance recoveries related to the fires were 519 through the end of the quarter (RQ2 page:1). - Net debt is a company definition: long-term debt, current portion, short-term borrowings and unamortized adjustments, less cash and cash equivalents (RQ2 page:10). It equals principal debt less cash. Restricted cash of 7 is not netted and operating lease liabilities are not included in debt. - The trailing twelve month column is the company's own construction: fiscal year, less the prior six months, plus the current six months (RQ2 page:9). - ABL fixed charge coverage test: the annual report states a minimum of 1.25 to 1.0 that applies "if an event of default has occurred and is continuing and/or excess availability is less than the greater of (1) $150 million and (2) 10% of the lesser of the total ABL Revolver commitment and the borrowing base" (AR page:148). The company reports compliance at September 30, 2026 (Q2R page:18). The June 16, 2026 amendment changed the ABL; its covenant text is not supplied, so headroom is shown in Calculations as an indication only.

facts.label: Evidence, mechanism and credit implication
facts.text: - Evidence: debt rose by 1,819 in six months to 9,797 and short-term borrowings doubled to 2,631 (calculated, see Calculations). Mechanism: capital spending and working capital were funded mainly from the revolver, whose availability is limited by the lesser of the commitment and the borrowing base (AR page:148); the composition of the borrowing base is not printed in the pages read. Implication: remaining availability of 606 is the main committed backstop and is exposed to revolver usage and to any borrowing base movement. - Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA of 1,831 trailing is built on exclusions of 257 of metal price lag deduction, 236 of fire losses and 44 of start-up costs in the six months. Mechanism: some exclusions lower the measure (metal price lag) and others raise it (fire losses, start-up costs), and the start-up exclusion ends when the plant reaches normal capacity. Implication: the reported 4.7x is definition-sensitive, and the gross ratio of 5.35x should be read alongside it. - Evidence: the 3.25% notes due November 2026 are 13 and the nearest large note maturities are in 2029 and 2030. Mechanism: refinancing risk in the notes is concentrated beyond the next two years, but the revolver, Brazil and other short-term borrowings of 2,631 are classified as due within one year. Implication: near-term refinancing risk sits in bank lines, not the bonds. - Evidence: cash interest is printed only annually. Mechanism: interim coverage cannot be computed on a cash basis. Implication: coverage is shown only for fiscal years.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Novelis Inc. is a Canadian-incorporated, Atlanta-headquartered producer of aluminum rolled products that is wholly owned indirectly by Hindalco Industries Ltd. and files as a voluntary filer without public equity (AR page:1; page:2). Its model converts purchased primary and recycled metal into sheet, plate and foil for beverage packaging, automotive, aerospace and specialty customers, and passes metal price through to customers under a three-part price of an LME base, a local market premium and a conversion premium (AR page:73), so margin per tonne rather than metal price is the economic driver, and the open exposure is the timing difference called metal price lag (AR page:74). The creditor-relevant business facts are three. First, revenue is concentrated: the 10 largest customers were 57% of fiscal 2026 net sales against 41% in fiscal 2025, and one customer, Ball, was 18% (AR page:33; page:188). Second, the company is in the middle of a capital programme centered on a greenfield plant in Bay Minette, Alabama that management sizes at approximately 5.0 billion (AR page:72) and that the company says is funded through cash flows from operations and "a combination of local financing, our senior secured credit facilities, equity contributions from our common shareholder, and senior notes" (Q2R page:61), which is consistent with the rise in leverage and revolver usage shown in the financial base. Third, two fires at the Oswego plant in September and November 2025 idled the Oswego hot mill until its restart in early June 2026 and management estimated a total negative cash flow impact of approximately 1.7 billion before insurance (AR page:70; Q2R page:36); cumulative net insurance recoveries were 519 through September 30, 2026 (Q2R page:48). Ownership behavior in the filings is supportive on equity (950 of subscriptions at 150 a share in fiscal 2026) and mixed on distributions (a 35 return of capital in fiscal 2026 and a new brand royalty to an affiliate), and the filings give no signal of creditor-adverse transactions such as priming or drop-downs; that absence is an observation about the pages read, not proof of the legal capacity to do them, which depends on indenture and credit agreement terms that were not supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Financing activity over the last two fiscal years is a sequence of completed refinancings and new money for the Bay Minette programme, all described in the debt note. In fiscal 2025 the company issued 750 of 6.875% Senior Notes due January 2030 through Novelis Corporation and used the net proceeds to repay 738 of borrowings under the asset-based revolver (AR page:151), and entered a floating rate Term Loan Facility that provided 1,250 of proceeds and matures March 2032 (AR page:85; Q2R page:18); in September 2025 the term loan margin was cut from 2.00% to 1.75% over three-month Term SOFR (Q2R page:18). On August 18, 2025 Novelis Corporation issued 750 of 6.375% Senior Notes due August 2033 and used the net proceeds to buy 737 of the 750 outstanding 3.25% Senior Notes due November 2026 in a cash tender, leaving 13 outstanding (Q2R page:20; page:17). The Baldwin County Industrial Development Authority issued tax-exempt bonds loaned to Novelis Corporation to fund the Bay Minette plant: Series 2025A of 400 in June 2025 at 5.00%, Series 2025B of 100 in September 2025 at 4.625% and Series 2026A of 225 in March 2026 at 4.30%, each with a mandatory tender (June 2032 or March 2033) before final maturity (Q2R page:22 to page:24). The asset-based revolver was enlarged by 500 on February 19, 2026 to 2.5 billion and by a further 500 on June 16, 2026 to 3.0 billion, with maturity extended to June 16, 2031 (Q2R page:18). On July 23, 2026 the company signed an unsecured 500 term loan, fully drawn, due July 24, 2028 at Term SOFR plus 1.00% rising to 1.25% on certain rating events (Q2R page:21). Uncommitted trade and bank lines were added: a Citi facility of up to 300 after a January 2026 increase from 200, and an MUFG facility of up to 500 from May 26, 2026, both undrawn at September 30, 2026 (Q2R page:19). Use of proceeds disclosed: bonds and the Bay Minette related issuance for construction costs, the 2033 notes for the tender of the 2026 notes, the March 2025 term loan to repay earlier term loans, and the 6.875% notes to repay revolver borrowings (Q2R page:18; page:20; page:22; AR page:151). The use of proceeds for the July 2026 term loan is Insufficient Information in the pages read.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability. Evidence: supply contracts of "one to five years", a stated "high degree of renewal business" and significant switching costs (AR page:23) against a top 10 customer share of 57% in fiscal 2026 from 41% (AR page:33). Mechanism: long contracts and qualification costs support volume visibility, but a few customers hold most of the volume, so one non-renewal or insourcing decision moves a large share of revenue. Implication: revenue is durable in the base case and lumpy in the downside; the leverage tolerance of the credit is lower than the stable sector profile suggests. - Margin and earnings quality. Evidence: price pass-through under the conversion model (AR page:73) and adjustments for metal price lag, fire losses and start-up costs inside Adjusted EBITDA (RQ4 page:9). Mechanism: pass-through protects conversion margin against metal price moves, but timing gains and losses, fire items and start-up costs are excluded from the measure, so the measure and cash earnings can differ by large amounts in a period. Implication: leverage computed on Adjusted EBITDA should be read with the exclusions; the financial base carries both. - Cash flow and liquidity. Evidence: capital spending guidance of 2.1 to 2.4 billion for fiscal 2027 (Q2R page:48), negative operating cash flow for the six months (Q2R page:4) and revolver availability of 606 (Q2R page:19). Mechanism: the build continues for the rest of the year and start-up costs continue until normal capacity, while insurance recoveries are uncertain in amount and timing. Implication: refinancing and liquidity depend on revolver access and on delivery of management's expected return to positive free cash flow, which is a management expectation (RQ2 page:3). - Sponsor alignment. Evidence: 950 of equity contributions and no fiscal 2027 distribution, against a new affiliate royalty. Mechanism: the parent has put in cash when the programme needed it; there is no stated obligation. Implication: treat parent support as demonstrated behavior, not a credit enhancement; the pages read contain no parent guarantee. - Key uncertainties: timing of Bay Minette commercial shipments, the amount and timing of remaining Oswego insurance recoveries, the effect of tariffs and duties (including a customs matter in which the company carries a cash deposit of approximately 127 for antidumping duties it is appealing, Q2R page:39), a union strike at the Yeongju plant that management says may affect beverage packaging shipments (Q2R page:47), and the absence of executed financing documents.

facts.label: Conflicts
facts.text: One internal inconsistency is logged and not reconciled. The annual report debt table lists "Series 2026A Bonds, due June 2033" (AR page:145) while its footnote says the bonds have "a mandatory tender for purchase on March 1, 2033" (AR page:145) and the Q2 quarterly report table lists "Series 2026A Bonds, due March 2033" (Q2R page:17). The amount is 225 and the difference is one quarter in the tender date label; the financial base used the later report's maturity buckets, which do not depend on the label. Two differences of basis are noted so they are not mistaken for conflicts. Total shipments of 3,731 kt in the annual report business section include affiliates on a proportionately consolidated basis and intersegment sales (AR page:20; page:21), while the release reports rolled product shipments of 3,557 kt for the same fiscal year (RQ4 page:1); they are different measures. Segment net sales add to more than consolidated net sales for the same reason (AR page:20; AR page:21).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Novelis Inc. is a large, diversified aluminum rolling credit whose leverage and liquidity have weakened over the past six months, but it complies with its covenants and has no bond maturity of size before April 2029. The strongest support is a conversion pricing model that passes metal cost to customers, scale across four regions and a trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,831 million. The weakest point is USD 9,797 million of debt, net leverage of 4.7x against a stated goal of 3.5x, USD 2,631 million of short-term borrowings and liquidity down to USD 2,038 million. The outcome turns on whether Bay Minette reaches commercial shipments, capital spending falls and insurance recoveries arrive, so that free cash flow turns positive.
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Novelis Inc. has become more leveraged because it is funding a USD 5.0 billion plant and recovering from two fires at the same time. Company-defined net leverage was 2.9x at March 31, 2025, 4.1x at March 31, 2026 and 4.7x at September 30, 2026, against a management goal of about 3.5x during the investment cycle, which management says tariffs and the fire impacts have pushed above target [financial base; Q2R p65]. Total debt rose by USD 1,819 million in six months to USD 9,797 million, and Adjusted Net Debt rose by USD 1,796 million, almost the same as the USD 1,804 million Adjusted Free Cash Flow outflow, so the extra debt is the cash burn of capital spending and working capital rather than shareholder returns [financial base; RQ2 p9, p10].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity has narrowed and rests on one facility. The company had USD 2,038 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026, down from USD 2,756 million at March 31, 2026, and the revolver availability of USD 606 million is the main committed backstop [financial base; Q2R p19, p61]. The reported figures reconcile to a revolver drawn about USD 2,266 million with USD 128 million of letters of credit against a USD 3,000 million commitment (calculated, see Calculations), which suggests the commitment rather than the borrowing base is the binding limit; that is an inference and the borrowing base is not printed. Short-term borrowings of USD 2,631 million are classified as due within one year, although the revolver itself matures on June 16, 2031 [Q2R p17, p18].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Bond maturities are not the near-term pressure. Only USD 13 million of 3.25% notes falls due in November 2026, and the next large maturities are USD 568 million of notes in April 2029, USD 2,350 million across two series in January 2030 and USD 750 million in August 2031 [financial base; Q2R p17]. The term loans mature in March 2032 and a USD 500 million term loan in July 2028. The risk is therefore the cost and availability of bank liquidity through the build, and then the size of the 2029 and 2030 refinancing if leverage has not come down.

facts.text: Earnings are improving on a reported basis but are definition sensitive. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA is USD 1,831 million against USD 1,645 million for fiscal 2026, and the quarter included USD 39 million of business interruption recoveries and favorable scrap effects that management cites [financial base; RQ2 p2]. The measure excludes USD 69 million of trailing start-up costs and USD 1,140 million of trailing fire losses net of recoveries, and deducts USD 574 million of trailing metal price lag; unadjusted EBITDA is USD 1,058 million [RQ2 p8, p9]. Management says it will stop excluding start-up costs once Bay Minette reaches normal capacity [Q2R p68].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Scale and diversification support business risk: 29 facilities in nine countries, four segments that all contributed positive Adjusted EBITDA, and fiscal 2026 net sales of USD 18,434 million across beverage packaging, automotive, aerospace and specialty markets [business context; AR p8, p188]. The conversion model passes aluminum price to customers, so margin per tonne rather than metal price drives earnings [AR p73]. Recycling gives a metal cost lever: the company purchased or tolled about 2,155 kt of recycled aluminum against 1,298 kt of primary in fiscal 2026 [AR p18]. The company is current on all covenants and reports compliance with each facility at September 30, 2026 [Q2R p18 to p24]. The financial maintenance covenant package described is light: a single springing test on the revolver, with negative covenants in the notes and term loans and no other maintenance ratio described in the pages read [AR p146 to p148; Q2R p19]. Debt maturities are staggered, with no bond of size due before April 2029 [financial base]. The parent put in USD 950 million of equity in fiscal 2026 and has paid no return of capital this fiscal year [business context]. The efficiency plan had delivered over USD 200 million of run-rate savings at fiscal 2026 year end against a target of USD 350 million to USD 400 million by fiscal 2028 [Q2R p47].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Net leverage of 4.7x is above management's 3.5x goal and gross debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 5.35x (calculated) [financial base]. Free cash flow is deeply negative: trailing Adjusted Free Cash Flow is an outflow of USD 3,682 million and operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 418 million in six months [financial base]. Liquidity is concentrated in a revolver that is mostly drawn, and short-term borrowings of USD 2,631 million exceed cash of USD 1,277 million [financial base]. Interim cash interest is not disclosed, and accrual interest expense rose to USD 80 million in the quarter from USD 68 million [Q2R p3]. Customer concentration is high and rose year on year [AR p33]. Execution risk is live: the Bay Minette cold mill produced its first coil in September 2026, but commercial shipments are only targeted for the first quarter of fiscal 2028, so start-up costs and capital spending continue before the plant earns [RQ2 p2]. Insurance recoveries of USD 519 million cumulatively are real but further amounts and timing are uncertain [Q2R p48]. Trade measures matter: tariffs reduced fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA by USD 143 million per the release, and the company announced a temporary production and staffing reduction at its Kingston, Canada plant because of duties [RQ4 p1; Q2R p47]. Floating rate debt exposes pre-tax income to about USD 15 million for each 100 basis points, on the company's stated sensitivity [Q2R p73]. Finally, the evidence on guarantee scope, covenant capacity and ratings is summary-level because no executed agreements or rating reports were supplied [source readiness].

facts.text: At September 30, 2026 cash was USD 1,277 million and availability under committed facilities USD 761 million, of which the revolver was USD 606 million with USD 128 million of letters of credit drawn on it [financial base; Q2R p19, p61]. The remaining USD 155 million of committed availability is not itemized in the pages read. Uncommitted Citi and MUFG facilities of up to USD 300 million and USD 500 million were undrawn and are not counted [Q2R p19]. Against this, USD 2,704 million of debt is due within one year, but USD 2,266 million of it is revolver borrowing (calculated) that matures in 2031 and USD 350 million is Brazil short-term loans, so the year-one figure is a rollover question rather than a scheduled repayment. Management's capital spending guidance of USD 2,100 million to USD 2,400 million for fiscal 2027 against USD 1,543 million spent in six months implies USD 557 million to USD 857 million in the second half (calculated). Operating cash flow for the second half is not guided in the filings, so no runway is computed. Seasonal or working capital swings matter: inventories rose to USD 5,145 million from USD 4,401 million and supplier finance programs hold USD 1.5 billion of confirmed invoices in payables [Q2R p3, p8].

facts.label: Liquidity and refinancing
facts.text: Covenant position. The notes and the term loans carry negative covenants and a cross-acceleration or cross-default feature; the Term Loan Facility cross-defaults to the revolver regardless of amount [Q2R p19, p20; AR p146]. Compliance is reported for every facility at September 30, 2026. The revolver springing fixed charge test is 1.25 to 1.0 and the company's own reported figure for it is not given; headroom cannot be stated, only that availability is above the highest the trigger can be [AR p148; financial base].

facts.label: Structure and claims outside debt
facts.text: Secured debt under the senior secured credit facilities is the term loans of USD 1,231 million and the revolver of about USD 2,266 million, together USD 3,497 million (calculated), secured by substantially all assets of the company and the guarantors [AR p146]. The senior notes of USD 4,431 million and the tax-exempt bonds of USD 725 million are senior unsecured and guaranteed by Novelis Inc. and certain subsidiaries (calculated) [Q2R p17, p19, p22]; the USD 500 million 2026 term loan is unsecured, and its guarantors are not stated in the pages read [Q2R p21]. Non-guarantor subsidiaries held USD 3.7 billion of assets and USD 2.2 billion of debt and other liabilities including intercompany balances at September 30, 2026 [Q2R p65], which rank structurally ahead of the notes as to those subsidiaries' assets, although the figure includes intercompany balances. Outside the debt figure the company has operating lease liabilities of USD 112 million at March 31, 2026, accrued postretirement benefits of USD 449 million, estimated benefit payments of USD 1.2 billion through 2036, purchase obligations of USD 17.2 billion at March 31, 2026 of which USD 7.6 billion fall due within 12 months, supplier finance of USD 1.5 billion inside payables, factoring whose volume is not printed, and a cash deposit of about USD 127 million held against disputed U.S. antidumping duties [financial base; AR p84; Q2R p8, p39].

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filed documents are sufficient for the financial base, business context, credit synthesis and evidence trace of Novelis Inc., with bounded limits. No source is blocked, and the latest quarter is covered. | High | No executed debt agreements, no rating agency material and no earnings slides were supplied; guarantor detail is only summarized. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The annual report and three quarterly reports give audited and unaudited statements, debt notes, liquidity and segment tables through the latest quarter. | Debt, liquidity and earnings work can start from filed statements, which control over management narrative. | High |

| Debt instruments have different legal issuers, while Novelis Inc. is consolidated registrant and guarantor of the notes; only summaries of the guarantee terms are supplied. | Structural position and guarantee scope cannot be confirmed from executed documents. | Medium |

| Covenant terms are described only in note summaries; the asset-based revolver was amended after the annual report. | Maintenance tests and headroom must carry the amendment and the lack of agreement text as limits. | Medium |
| No rating agency report, market quote or earnings slide deck is in the pack. | Ratings, pricing and relative value cannot be sourced here; management claims rest on the releases alone. | High |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is ready with limitations for all four requested consumers. Every supplied document is an SEC filing or an exhibit to one, so original authority sits with the filed statements and notes, and the three earnings releases are attributed management narrative that cannot override them. The newest periodic filing covers the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and was signed on the cutoff date, and the newest release carries the same date, so the latest quarter and the subsequent-events window up to the cutoff are covered. No source has blocked preparation and none is used as a fallback for another. The strongest contrary evidence is the absence of executed legal documents, rating agency material, market data and presentation slides, together with the fact that the debt, guarantee and covenant terms reach this review only through note summaries and exhibit index entries. That keeps legal questions about who issued, who guarantees and what is tested at the level of attributed summary, and it limits ratings and relative-value work to what the filings state. Source sufficiency is established here; no figure has been normalized or reconciled, and downstream modules must still do that against the cited pages.
### Source-by-source assessment
**Annual report, fiscal 2026 (10-K).**

- Identity and perimeter: the cover prints "Novelis Inc. (Exact name of registrant as specified in its charter)" and the period "For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026" (page:1). It states "The registrant is a voluntary filer" (page:1) and "All of the registrant's outstanding shares were held indirectly by Hindalco Industries Ltd., the registrant's parent company." (page:2). The context leaves the parent blank; the filing names Hindalco as parent, so the context blank is an input gap and not evidence of no parent.

- Statements and notes present: income statement, balance sheet and cash flow are on pages 110 to 112; the cash flow page prints "Interest paid $ 242 $ 247 $ 279" (page:112). Debt note on pages 145 to 154, retirement benefits on pages 158 to 163, commitments and contingencies from page 181, segment information from page 184, and Item 7 liquidity discussion on pages 82 to 87.

- Guarantor perimeter: page:86 carries a "Non-Guarantor Information" block giving the non-guarantor share of net sales, Adjusted EBITDA and assets, and the exhibit index (page:206) names instrument-level issuers, for example "Novelis Sheet Ingot GmbH, as issuer" for the 3.375% notes due 2029.

- Version relationship: the Q2 fiscal 2027 quarterly report refers to an "Amendment No. 1 on Form 10-K/A" filed on June 17, 2026 (page:75 of the Q2 quarterly report, text: "Amendment No. 1 on Form 10-K/A to the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on June 17, 2026"). That amendment is not in the pack. The annual report's own page range includes Part III (directors and officers, pages 190 to 205), so the missing amendment is not needed for the financial or debt facts.

**Quarterly report, fiscal Q3 2026 (10-Q for December 31, 2025).** Cover period "For the quarterly period ended December 31, 2025" (page:1). It gives the discrete quarter and nine-month statements, the debt note and an exhibit index entry for the September 2025 ABL amendment, exhibit 4.5, "Amendment No. 1 to Credit Agreement, dated as of September 16, 2025, by and among, Novelis Holdings Inc. as Borrower, Novelis Inc. as Intermediate Holdings" (page:78). It also states "We utilized $131 million of the ABL Revolver for letters of credit." (page:19). It is a distinct, still active period record; the later reports do not replace it for the December 2025 quarter.

**Quarterly report, fiscal Q1 2027 (10-Q for June 30, 2026).** Cover period "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026" (page:1). Statements are on pages 3 to 5, debt on pages 15 to 21, MD&A liquidity on pages 55 to 58, and Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation on pages 59 to 61. It carries prior-year comparatives for the quarter ended June 30, 2025, which is the only supplied source for that discrete quarter.

**Quarterly report, fiscal Q2 2027 (10-Q for September 30, 2026).** Cover period "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026" (page:1). It is the latest periodic filing and the controlling source for current debt, liquidity and covenant status. The statement of operations is headed "Three Months Ended September 30, Six Months Ended September 30," (page:3). The debt table prints "Total debt $ 9,797 $ (63) $ 9,734 $ 7,978 $ (68) $ 7,910" (page:17) and a maturity table by year follows on the same page. Page:61 prints "Availability under committed credit facilities 761 1,502". It is also the only supplied source for the discrete quarter ended September 30, 2025 (as comparative) and the six months to September 30, 2025. Part II Item 5 reports board changes dated November 3, 2026 (page:74), a subsequent-period item inside the cutoff.

**Earnings release, fiscal Q4 2026 (May 19, 2026).** The only supplied source for the discrete fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 (the annual report gives the year; the Q3 report gives nine months). Headline: "Net loss attributable to our common shareholder of $84 million" (page:1). Management narrative and non-GAAP reconciliations are attributed supporting claims, to be tied to the annual report where both state a figure.

**Earnings release, fiscal Q1 2027 (August 5, 2026).** States "Total liquidity stood at $2.1 billion as of June 30, 2026" (page:3). Attributed management narrative; reconciles to the Q1 quarterly report.

**Earnings release, fiscal Q2 2027 (November 5, 2026).** Headline "Adjusted EBITDA of $508 million, up 20% YoY" (page:1); states "Total liquidity stood at $2.0 billion as of September 30, 2026" (page:2); the Net Leverage Ratio table prints "Net Leverage Ratio 4.7 4.1" for September 30, 2026 and March 31, 2026 (page:10). It supplies the trailing-twelve-month column, built as the note on page:9 describes: "The amounts in the TTM column are calculated by taking the amounts for the year ended March 31, 2026, subtracting the amounts for the six months ended September 30, 2025, and adding the amounts for the six months ended September 30, 2026." The release is dated on the cutoff date and is inside it.
### Coverage and extraction

- All seven extraction files were opened. Every page of each was indexed by its opening text and located by section, and the pages named above were read in full. This is a coverage inventory by located section, not a page-by-page fidelity review; extraction success is not treated as fidelity.

- The extraction is flattened text. Tables are kept as row strings with spaces between cells, with column headers retained on the page where the table starts. Multi-column period headers were readable in every table opened. A page split can separate a table from its footnote; for example the debt table starts on page:16 and continues on page:17 of the Q2 quarterly report. Downstream modules must open both pages.

- No images, charts, speaker notes or workbooks are in the pack. The releases refer to presentation slides ("This news release and the presentation slides for the earnings call contain non-GAAP financial measures as defined by SEC rules.", Q2 release page:4), and the slides are not supplied. That is a parse gap for slide content, not a claim about it.
- Inline XBRL data files are listed in the exhibit indexes but are not in the pack, so statement values come from the text extraction only.
### Currency, units, periods and basis
- Reporting currency is USD and statement amounts are in millions of USD ("in millions" headers, for example page:61 of the Q2 quarterly report). The context currency and the filings agree.

- Debt includes foreign-currency borrowings stated in USD equivalents with the local amount in the note text, for example "CNY 140 million" (Q2 quarterly report, page:20) and "CHF 100 million" (page:21). Conversion basis is "using exchange rates as of September 30, 2026" (page:17).

- The fiscal year ends March 31. The context labels q2-2027 and fy-2026 map to the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and the year ended March 31, 2026. Filings use "fiscal 2026" and "fiscal 2027" in the same sense, with the convention footnote on page:3 of the Q2 quarterly report. No calendar-year label may be applied to these figures.

- Quarter versus year-to-date: Q2 fiscal 2027 and six-month figures sit side by side in the same tables; the Q3 report mixes three and nine months; the Q4 release mixes three months and twelve months. Downstream modules must label each figure with its basis.

- Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Free Cash Flow, Adjusted Net Debt and the Net Leverage Ratio are management non-GAAP measures defined in the segment note and the release reconciliations, not filed GAAP statement lines.
### Version relationships and conflicts
- The four periodic filings are distinct period records and are all retained. None is a duplicate of another. No file hash is shared across the seven sources.

- Supersession by dated events, not a conflict: the annual report prints "The ABL Revolver matures on August 18, 2027" (page:148), while the Q2 quarterly report records an amendment on June 16, 2026 that increased availability "to an aggregate total of $3.0 billion and to extend the maturity until June 16, 2031" (page:18). The amendment post-dates the fiscal year end, so the later filing controls current terms and the annual report controls the March 31, 2026 position.

- The annual report states the fixed charge coverage test as "maintaining a specified minimum fixed charge coverage ratio of 1.25 to 1.0" with conditions (page:148). The Q2 quarterly report states compliance with covenants of each facility (pages 18 to 22) but does not restate the test, so the test text is carried from the annual report, with the June 2026 amendment as an open limitation.

- Release versus filing: the Q2 release says liquidity is $2.0 billion and the Q2 quarterly report prints a table with a total (page:61); the two sources are consistent in scale, and the release rounds. No figure conflict was found in the inputs read; no cross-source reconciliation was run, by design.

- The ABL availability in the debt note and the total committed availability in the liquidity table are different measures; the split of the committed availability by facility is a downstream task and is carried as a gap below.
### Entity roles found in the sources
- Registrant, consolidated reporting entity and guarantor of the notes: Novelis Inc.
- Indirect parent: Hindalco Industries Ltd., through AV Minerals (Netherlands) N.V. (Q2 quarterly report page:16: "indirectly through Hindalco's subsidiary, AV Minerals (Netherlands) N.V.").

- Note issuers differ by instrument. Q2 quarterly report page:20: "Novelis Corporation, a wholly owned subsidiary of Novelis Inc., issued $750 million in aggregate principal amount of the 2033 Senior Notes". The annual report exhibit index names Novelis Corporation as issuer for several series and Novelis Sheet Ingot GmbH for the 3.375% notes (page:206). The tax-exempt bonds were issued by the Baldwin IDA and loaned to Novelis Corporation (Q2 quarterly report pages:22 and 23).

- Guarantee description: "are guaranteed, jointly and severally, on a senior unsecured basis, by Novelis Inc. and certain of its subsidiaries" (Q2 quarterly report page:19). The list of guarantors is not in the supplied pages; the share of non-guarantors is: "Net sales represented by non-guarantor subsidiaries (for the six months ended September 30, 2026) 20 %" (page:64).

- ABL Revolver parties are named only in the exhibit index: Novelis Holdings Inc. as borrower and Novelis Inc. as Intermediate Holdings (Q3 fiscal 2026 quarterly report, page:78). The restricted or unrestricted status of entities is not stated beyond the indenture covenant summary.
### Consumer assessments
| Consumer | Status | Evidence demand | Carried limitations |

| CP-1 financial base | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Discrete quarters, fiscal years, quarter and year-to-date, segments, add-backs, KPIs, facility-level debt, cash interest and tax: all located (annual report pages 110 to 112 and 145 to 154; Q2 report pages 3 to 5, 17 to 23, 40 to 44; release pages 9 to 11). | Discrete Q1 and Q2 fiscal 2026 come only from comparative columns of the fiscal 2027 reports; the source reports for those quarters are not in the pack. Text-flattened tables. Management non-GAAP measures. SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; model input contract not evaluated. |

| CP-1A business and transaction | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description, segments, Oswego fires and insurance, Bay Minette plant, financing events, related party and parent transactions: located in the annual report (pages 8 to 29, 70 to 72, 174) and the latest quarterly report and release. | Slides not supplied; no executed transaction documents; forward-looking statements are management claims; the 10-K/A is not in the pack. |

| CP-2 credit synthesis | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Debt, maturities, liquidity, covenant status, leverage, guarantor shares, retirement obligations, leases, supply chain finance and factoring: located in the notes and MD&A. | No agreement text for any facility or indenture; guarantor list not supplied; no rating agency material; no market quotes; covenant test text predates the June 2026 ABL amendment; facility split of committed availability needs downstream work. |

| CP-5 evidence trace | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Page-level locators exist in all seven files and every material claim can be traced to a page. | The pinned hash identifies the extraction, not the original HTML; fidelity of the extraction to the original is unreviewed. Dependent on the accuracy of upstream handoffs, which do not exist yet. |
None of the four is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. A missing downstream handoff is not treated as a source condition.
### Evidence, risk mechanism and downstream consequence

- Evidence: debt is described in a table plus per-instrument paragraphs, while legal terms are only summarized and the indentures and credit agreement are only listed as exhibits (annual report pages 206 to 208). Risk mechanism: a summary can omit baskets, definitions and release conditions that decide guarantee coverage and covenant headroom. Consequence: CP-2 must label guarantee and covenant statements as summary-level and may not state headroom beyond the percentages and tests that the filings print.

- Evidence: the parent is Hindalco and the context names none. Risk mechanism: a perimeter built from the context alone would drop parent support, related-party flows and equity contributions. Consequence: CP-1A and CP-2 must take the parent role from the filings and keep parent figures out of the issuer's statements.

- Evidence: short-term borrowings and the ABL are described together with an ABL amendment after the annual report. Risk mechanism: using the annual report terms for current availability or maturity would misstate the facility. Consequence: CP-2 uses the Q2 quarterly report for current terms and the annual report only for March 31, 2026.

- Evidence: the releases are management documents dated within days of the filings. Risk mechanism: a release figure can differ in rounding or definition from the filing. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-5 cite the filing where both state a figure and use the release only for attributed non-GAAP measures.
## Calculations
No financial figure was calculated, normalized or reconciled in this module, as the method requires. The only counts are coverage counts of supplied pages, taken from the extraction files:
| Count | Inputs | Result |
| Total supplied pages | 210 + 78 + 69 + 76 + 11 + 11 + 11 | 466 pages in seven files |
| Periodic filing pages | 210 + 78 + 69 + 76 | 433 pages |
| Release pages | 11 + 11 + 11 | 33 pages |

Coverage statement: 466 of 466 pages were indexed and located by section; the pages cited in this document were read in full. Pages not cited were not read line by line, and no claim of full-text fidelity review is made.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation | Evidence |

| Executed debt documents not supplied: indentures, the credit agreements and the guaranty agreements are listed in exhibit indexes only. The context sets legal documents to none. | High | CP-2, CP-5 | Obtain the executed agreements, or label every term as filing summary. | Annual report page:206 to page:208; Q3 fiscal 2026 quarterly report page:78 |

| Guarantor list and guarantor-level financials not supplied; only the percentage shares of net sales, Adjusted EBITDA and assets held by non-guarantors are printed. | Medium | CP-2 | Treat the structure as summary-level; do not compute guarantor coverage. | Annual report page:86; Q2 quarterly report page:64 |

| Covenant test text for the ABL revolver is from the annual report, and the ABL was amended on June 16, 2026. Financial covenant levels for the other facilities are described as customary without levels. | Medium | CP-2 | Carry the amendment as a limitation; do not state headroom for tests the filings do not quantify. | Annual report page:148; Q2 quarterly report pages 18 to 22 |

| No rating agency report, rating, outlook or market quote is in the pack, and the context ratings and quotes are empty. Rating mentions in the filings concern indenture covenant suspension, a loan margin step and risk factors. | Medium | CP-2 and later relative-value work | Ratings stay Not supplied. | Q2 quarterly report pages 20 and 21 |
| Earnings presentation slides are referred to but not supplied. | Low | CP-1A, CP-2 | Slide content stays unparsed; releases serve as the attributed source. | Q2 release page:4 |

| The Form 10-K/A filed June 17, 2026 is not supplied. | Low | CP-1A | Part III content is in the annual report; check the amendment only if director compensation is needed. | Q2 quarterly report page:75 |

| Quarterly reports for June 30, 2025 and September 30, 2025 are not in the pack; those quarters come from comparative columns in fiscal 2027 reports. | Low | CP-1 | Cite the comparative column and its report; note any later reclassification only if a filing says so. | Q1 and Q2 fiscal 2027 quarterly reports, pages 3 to 5 |

| Facility-level split of the committed availability reported in the liquidity table is not shown in the liquidity table itself; the debt note gives ABL availability separately. | Low | CP-2 | Reconcile in CP-2 from the debt note; do not infer facilities not named. | Q2 quarterly report pages 19 and 61 |

| Context leaves parent, borrower and guarantors blank, while the filings name a parent and instrument-level issuers. | Low | CP-1A, CP-2 | Use the filings for roles; the context is not evidence. | Annual report pages 2 and 206 |

| Original HTML tables, inline XBRL facts, images and charts are not in the pack; the extraction is flattened text. | Low | CP-1, CP-5 | Cite page locators; report any table whose layout is ambiguous. | All seven files |
| Pre-cutoff status: no source in the pack is dated after the cutoff. The latest items are dated on the cutoff date. | None | All | No action. | Q2 release and Q2 quarterly report |
## Next module

Run CP-1 next, on the fiscal Q2 2027 quarterly report as the controlling source for current figures, the annual report for fiscal 2026, and the Q3 fiscal 2026 and Q1 fiscal 2027 reports and the three releases for discrete quarters. It must label each figure as quarter, six months, nine months, fiscal year or trailing twelve months, use USD in millions, open both pages of split tables, and carry the gaps above, namely summary-level legal terms, the unsupplied slides, the unsupplied 10-K/A and the absence of ratings and quotes. ### Financial base view

Novelis Inc. enters the latest quarter with higher leverage than a year earlier and thinner liquidity, while earnings are improving. Company-defined net leverage was 2.9x at March 31, 2025, 4.1x at March 31, 2026 and 4.7x at September 30, 2026 (RQ4 page:10; RQ2 page:10). The rise comes from the numerator: total debt principal grew from 6,212 at March 31, 2025 to 7,978 at March 31, 2026 and 9,797 at September 30, 2026 (AR page:145; Q2R page:17), while cash was 1,036, 1,254 and 1,277 at the same dates and trailing Adjusted EBITDA moved from 1,802 to 1,645 to 1,831. Cash used in operations was negative 418 in the six months ended September 30, 2026 against positive 411 a year earlier, and capital expenditure was 1,543 against 913 (Q2R page:4 to page:5), so the Bay Minette plant and the Oswego fires absorbed more cash than operations produced. The funding came from the asset-based revolver, which carried about 2.3 billion of borrowings at September 30, 2026 against 935 at March 31, 2026 (Q2R page:18 to page:19; AR page:146), a 500 term loan taken in July 2026 (Q2R page:21) and 950 of equity contributions from the parent in fiscal 2026 (AR page:111). Liquidity of 2,038 is 718 below the 2,756 at March 31, 2026; availability under committed facilities fell to 761 from 1,502 while cash rose to 1,277 from 1,254, and the filing attributes the decrease primarily to a higher revolver balance (Q2R page:61 to page:62). The latest quarter itself was strong on a reported basis: Adjusted EBITDA of 508 against 422 and net income of 210 against 163 (RQ2 page:9; Q2R page:3), but part of the Adjusted EBITDA gain is a 39 business interruption recovery and favorable metal and scrap effects that management itself cites (RQ2 page:2). Management expects capital spending to fall as Bay Minette moves to start-up and forecasts positive free cash flow and a start of deleveraging toward the end of fiscal 2027 (RQ2 page:3); that is a management expectation and is not used in any figure here.

### Definition review

- Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure. The reconciliation adds back or removes: metal price lag (a deduction of 515 in fiscal 2026 and of 257 in the six months ended September 30, 2026), Oswego fire losses net of recoveries (925 and 236), restructuring and impairment (195 and 24), start-up costs (38 and 44) and a proportional consolidation adjustment for the Logan joint venture (55 in fiscal 2026) (RQ4 page:9; RQ2 page:9; AR page:187). The fire add-back was negative 29 in the quarter, because recoveries exceeded charges.

- Start-up costs are excluded now, and the company states it "will cease excluding such start-up costs from its Adjusted EBITDA once normal production capacity is achieved at the Bay Minette plant" (Q2R page:68). All else equal, Adjusted EBITDA will then be lower than on the present definition; this is an inference from the stated change, not a company figure.

- Business interruption insurance recoveries of 39 are cited by management as a driver of the quarter's Adjusted EBITDA improvement (RQ2 page:2). Cumulative insurance recoveries related to the fires were 519 through the end of the quarter (RQ2 page:1).

- Net debt is a company definition: long-term debt, current portion, short-term borrowings and unamortized adjustments, less cash and cash equivalents (RQ2 page:10). It equals principal debt less cash. Restricted cash of 7 is not netted and operating lease liabilities are not included in debt.
- The trailing twelve month column is the company's own construction: fiscal year, less the prior six months, plus the current six months (RQ2 page:9).

- ABL fixed charge coverage test: the annual report states a minimum of 1.25 to 1.0 that applies "if an event of default has occurred and is continuing and/or excess availability is less than the greater of (1) $150 million and (2) 10% of the lesser of the total ABL Revolver commitment and the borrowing base" (AR page:148). The company reports compliance at September 30, 2026 (Q2R page:18). The June 16, 2026 amendment changed the ABL; its covenant text is not supplied, so headroom is shown in Calculations as an indication only.

### Evidence, mechanism and credit implication

- Evidence: debt rose by 1,819 in six months to 9,797 and short-term borrowings doubled to 2,631 (calculated, see Calculations). Mechanism: capital spending and working capital were funded mainly from the revolver, whose availability is limited by the lesser of the commitment and the borrowing base (AR page:148); the composition of the borrowing base is not printed in the pages read. Implication: remaining availability of 606 is the main committed backstop and is exposed to revolver usage and to any borrowing base movement.

- Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA of 1,831 trailing is built on exclusions of 257 of metal price lag deduction, 236 of fire losses and 44 of start-up costs in the six months. Mechanism: some exclusions lower the measure (metal price lag) and others raise it (fire losses, start-up costs), and the start-up exclusion ends when the plant reaches normal capacity. Implication: the reported 4.7x is definition-sensitive, and the gross ratio of 5.35x should be read alongside it.

- Evidence: the 3.25% notes due November 2026 are 13 and the nearest large note maturities are in 2029 and 2030. Mechanism: refinancing risk in the notes is concentrated beyond the next two years, but the revolver, Brazil and other short-term borrowings of 2,631 are classified as due within one year. Implication: near-term refinancing risk sits in bank lines, not the bonds.
- Evidence: cash interest is printed only annually. Mechanism: interim coverage cannot be computed on a cash basis. Implication: coverage is shown only for fiscal years.
### Correction and consistency with the upstream handoff

The upstream readiness handoff stated that the Q2 FY2027 release liquidity of 2.0 billion was consistent with the quarterly report table; that holds (2,038). It carried a gap that the facility split of committed availability was not itemized. This handoff partly closes it: the revolver reports 606 of availability and 128 of letters of credit at September 30, 2026 (Q2R page:19), and total committed availability is 761, so 155 of committed availability is not itemized in the pages read. No other upstream statement is corrected.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Novelis is a wholly owned subsidiary of Hindalco with a conversion business model, large customer concentration and a roughly 5.0 billion Bay Minette build now starting up. The parent has funded part of it with 950 of equity. | High | No executed financing documents, rating reports or transaction agreements were supplied, so control rights and distribution capacity are described only at filing-summary level. |

### Business and transaction view

Novelis Inc. is a Canadian-incorporated, Atlanta-headquartered producer of aluminum rolled products that is wholly owned indirectly by Hindalco Industries Ltd. and files as a voluntary filer without public equity (AR page:1; page:2). Its model converts purchased primary and recycled metal into sheet, plate and foil for beverage packaging, automotive, aerospace and specialty customers, and passes metal price through to customers under a three-part price of an LME base, a local market premium and a conversion premium (AR page:73), so margin per tonne rather than metal price is the economic driver, and the open exposure is the timing difference called metal price lag (AR page:74). The creditor-relevant business facts are three. First, revenue is concentrated: the 10 largest customers were 57% of fiscal 2026 net sales against 41% in fiscal 2025, and one customer, Ball, was 18% (AR page:33; page:188). Second, the company is in the middle of a capital programme centered on a greenfield plant in Bay Minette, Alabama that management sizes at approximately 5.0 billion (AR page:72) and that the company says is funded through cash flows from operations and "a combination of local financing, our senior secured credit facilities, equity contributions from our common shareholder, and senior notes" (Q2R page:61), which is consistent with the rise in leverage and revolver usage shown in the financial base. Third, two fires at the Oswego plant in September and November 2025 idled the Oswego hot mill until its restart in early June 2026 and management estimated a total negative cash flow impact of approximately 1.7 billion before insurance (AR page:70; Q2R page:36); cumulative net insurance recoveries were 519 through September 30, 2026 (Q2R page:48). Ownership behavior in the filings is supportive on equity (950 of subscriptions at 150 a share in fiscal 2026) and mixed on distributions (a 35 return of capital in fiscal 2026 and a new brand royalty to an affiliate), and the filings give no signal of creditor-adverse transactions such as priming or drop-downs; that absence is an observation about the pages read, not proof of the legal capacity to do them, which depends on indenture and credit agreement terms that were not supplied.
### Company and operating model
| Area | Facts | Category | Locator |

| Products and end markets | Fiscal 2026 net sales by end market: beverage packaging 10,038; specialty 3,959; automotive 3,707; aerospace and industrial plate 730; total 18,434 | Documentary Fact | AR page:188 |

| Geography | Four segments. Fiscal 2026 segment net sales including intersegment and proportional affiliates: North America 7,932; Europe 5,272; Asia 3,430; South America 2,861. Fiscal 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDA: 435, 379, 311 and 521 | Documentary Fact | AR page:20; AR page:187 |

| Customers | Direct sales to large fabricators and OEMs under supply contracts of generally one to five years; distributors 6% of net sales; Ball 18% of net sales in fiscal 2026 (17% in fiscal 2025, 14% in fiscal 2024); 10 largest customers 57%, 41% and 48% for fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024 | Documentary Fact | AR page:23; AR page:33; AR page:188 |

Metal price lag was a deduction of 515 from Adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2026 | Documentary Fact | AR page:74; RQ4 page:9 |

| Volume drivers | Rolled product shipments were 3,557 kt in fiscal 2026 and 1,835 kt in the six months ended September 30, 2026 against 1,904 kt a year earlier; the Q2 release cites higher beverage packaging and aerospace shipments offset by lower automotive and specialty | Documentary Fact | RQ4 page:1; RQ2 page:11; RQ2 page:2 |

| Cost structure | Cost of goods sold exclusive of depreciation and amortization was 15,587 of net sales of 18,434 in fiscal 2026; the company purchased or tolled about 1,298 kt of primary aluminum and 2,155 kt of recycled aluminum in fiscal 2026; energy is a major input | Documentary Fact | AR page:110; AR page:17; AR page:18 |

| Scrap and tariffs | Management cites tight scrap spreads in fiscal 2025 that improved afterwards, and tariffs; the fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA impact of tariffs was 143 per the release. In September 2026 the company announced a temporary production and staffing reduction at Kingston, Canada, over at least six months because of duties on Canadian aluminum entering the United States | Management Language | AR page:18; RQ4 page:1; Q2R page:47 |

| Capital spending | Capital expenditures were 2,343 in fiscal 2026 and 1,543 in the six months ended September 30, 2026; management expects 2.1 to 2.4 billion for fiscal 2027, of which about 350 is maintenance | Documentary Fact; guidance is Management Language | AR page:111; Q2R page:4; Q2R page:48 |

### Company profile
| Item | Facts | Category | Locator |

| Legal entity and perimeter | Novelis Inc., formed in Canada on September 21, 2004; consolidated registrant; some notes are issued by Novelis Corporation and Novelis Sheet Ingot GmbH and guaranteed by Novelis Inc. and certain subsidiaries | Documentary Fact | AR page:8; AR page:150; Q2R page:19; Q2R page:20 |

| Country and sector | Incorporated in Canada, headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia; sector per the run context is rolling, drawing and extruding of nonferrous metals (context, not issuer evidence) | Documentary Fact | AR page:1; AR page:8 |

| Ownership | All shares held indirectly by Hindalco Industries Ltd.: directly by AV Minerals (Netherlands) N.V. since the September 1, 2022 plan of arrangement; 606,333,333 common shares outstanding; no public market for the shares | Documentary Fact | AR page:2; AR page:8 |

Percentages beyond sole ownership, shareholder agreements and any parent guarantee: Insufficient Information, the supplied pages state none | Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information | Q2R page:74 |

| Equity support | Subscription agreements: 5,000,000 shares for 750 on December 23, 2025 and 1,333,333 shares for 200 on February 18, 2026, 150 a share, total 950 of equity contributions in fiscal 2026 | Documentary Fact | Q2R page:8; AR page:111 |
| Distributions | Return of capital of 35 in fiscal 2026 (first quarter) and 100 in fiscal 2024; none in the six months ended September 30, 2026 | Documentary Fact | AR page:111; Q2R page:16 |

| Related-party arrangements | Intellectual property license with Birla Group Holdings Private Limited effective July 1, 2026, royalty for fiscal 2027 not to exceed 24, with 11 expensed in the quarter; accounts payable to related parties 455 and receivables 295 at September 30, 2026; purchases of tolling services from the Alunorf affiliate | Documentary Fact | Q2R page:16; Q3R page:16 |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Financing activity over the last two fiscal years is a sequence of completed refinancings and new money for the Bay Minette programme, all described in the debt note. In fiscal 2025 the company issued 750 of 6.875% Senior Notes due January 2030 through Novelis Corporation and used the net proceeds to repay 738 of borrowings under the asset-based revolver (AR page:151), and entered a floating rate Term Loan Facility that provided 1,250 of proceeds and matures March 2032 (AR page:85; Q2R page:18); in September 2025 the term loan margin was cut from 2.00% to 1.75% over three-month Term SOFR (Q2R page:18). On August 18, 2025 Novelis Corporation issued 750 of 6.375% Senior Notes due August 2033 and used the net proceeds to buy 737 of the 750 outstanding 3.25% Senior Notes due November 2026 in a cash tender, leaving 13 outstanding (Q2R page:20; page:17). The Baldwin County Industrial Development Authority issued tax-exempt bonds loaned to Novelis Corporation to fund the Bay Minette plant: Series 2025A of 400 in June 2025 at 5.00%, Series 2025B of 100 in September 2025 at 4.625% and Series 2026A of 225 in March 2026 at 4.30%, each with a mandatory tender (June 2032 or March 2033) before final maturity (Q2R page:22 to page:24). The asset-based revolver was enlarged by 500 on February 19, 2026 to 2.5 billion and by a further 500 on June 16, 2026 to 3.0 billion, with maturity extended to June 16, 2031 (Q2R page:18). On July 23, 2026 the company signed an unsecured 500 term loan, fully drawn, due July 24, 2028 at Term SOFR plus 1.00% rising to 1.25% on certain rating events (Q2R page:21). Uncommitted trade and bank lines were added: a Citi facility of up to 300 after a January 2026 increase from 200, and an MUFG facility of up to 500 from May 26, 2026, both undrawn at September 30, 2026 (Q2R page:19). Use of proceeds disclosed: bonds and the Bay Minette related issuance for construction costs, the 2033 notes for the tender of the 2026 notes, the March 2025 term loan to repay earlier term loans, and the 6.875% notes to repay revolver borrowings (Q2R page:18; page:20; page:22; AR page:151). The use of proceeds for the July 2026 term loan is Insufficient Information in the pages read.

Equity and distributions: the parent subscribed 950 of new shares in fiscal 2026 for capital projects (AR page:86; Q2R page:8), the company returned 35 of capital to the parent in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 and has paid none in fiscal 2027 (Q2R page:16). The Aditya Birla brand license from July 1, 2026 is a new related-party cost of up to 24 for fiscal 2027 (Q2R page:16).

Operating events with transaction-like effects: the Oswego fires of September 16 and November 20, 2025, with the hot mill restarting in early June 2026 and cumulative net insurance recoveries of 519 through September 30, 2026 (Q2R page:36; page:48); the June 2024 Sierre flood in Switzerland, financed in part by a CHF 100 million loan from the Banque Cantonale du Valais whose interest is payable by the Canton of Valais (Q2R page:21); restructuring under the 2025 Efficiency Plan with cumulative costs of 185 and a target of approximately 350 to 400 of annualized savings by the end of fiscal 2028 (Q2R page:47); and the Bay Minette plant, whose cold mill produced its first coil in September 2026 with commercial shipments targeted for the first quarter of fiscal 2028 (RQ2 page:2). The annual report said the plant was expected to commission in fiscal 2027 and in the second half of calendar 2026 (AR page:2; page:72), while the Q2 release reports a first coil in September 2026 and targets commercial shipments in the first quarter of fiscal 2028. These are different milestones, commissioning and commercial shipments, so no delay is concluded and no conflict is logged.

Subsequent events within the cutoff, after the quarter ended September 30, 2026: the board changes of November 3, 2026 (Q2R page:74); the 13 balance of the 3.25% notes falls due on November 15, 2026 by contract (AR page:150; Q2R page:17), which is a scheduled maturity and not a reported event; and the Q2 results release of November 5, 2026. No acquisition, disposal, sponsor change, rating action or new debt issue dated after September 30, 2026 was found in the supplied sources. No pending transaction is described.
### Governance and sponsor behavior
| Behavior | Evidence | Category | Legal capacity, willingness, feasibility |

| Equity support: Supportive | 950 of subscriptions in fiscal 2026 to help fund capital projects (AR page:86) | Documentary Fact | Willingness shown by action; no legal commitment to continue is stated, and the filing says "There can be no assurances that similar funding from equity contributions from our common shareholder will be made available in the future" (Q2R page:61) |

| Distributions: Neutral or Mixed | Return of capital of 35 in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 while equity was also being contributed, none since (AR page:111; Q2R page:16) | Documentary Fact | Capacity under the notes: covenants limit dividends and restricted payments "beyond certain amounts" (Q2R page:19); the baskets are not supplied |

| Related-party leakage: Neutral or Mixed | Brand license royalty up to 24 for fiscal 2027 to an Aditya Birla Group company (Q2R page:16) | Documentary Fact | Approved by the board on August 4, 2026 (Q2R page:16); affiliate-transaction covenant text not supplied |

| Creditor-adverse actions | None found in the supplied pages: no priming, uptiering, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release is described | Insufficient Information | Cannot be excluded without the indentures and credit agreements; the unrestricted subsidiary designation right is mentioned in the covenant summary (Q2R page:19) |
### Credit translations

- Revenue durability. Evidence: supply contracts of "one to five years", a stated "high degree of renewal business" and significant switching costs (AR page:23) against a top 10 customer share of 57% in fiscal 2026 from 41% (AR page:33). Mechanism: long contracts and qualification costs support volume visibility, but a few customers hold most of the volume, so one non-renewal or insourcing decision moves a large share of revenue. Implication: revenue is durable in the base case and lumpy in the downside; the leverage tolerance of the credit is lower than the stable sector profile suggests.

- Margin and earnings quality. Evidence: price pass-through under the conversion model (AR page:73) and adjustments for metal price lag, fire losses and start-up costs inside Adjusted EBITDA (RQ4 page:9). Mechanism: pass-through protects conversion margin against metal price moves, but timing gains and losses, fire items and start-up costs are excluded from the measure, so the measure and cash earnings can differ by large amounts in a period. Implication: leverage computed on Adjusted EBITDA should be read with the exclusions; the financial base carries both.

- Cash flow and liquidity. Evidence: capital spending guidance of 2.1 to 2.4 billion for fiscal 2027 (Q2R page:48), negative operating cash flow for the six months (Q2R page:4) and revolver availability of 606 (Q2R page:19). Mechanism: the build continues for the rest of the year and start-up costs continue until normal capacity, while insurance recoveries are uncertain in amount and timing. Implication: refinancing and liquidity depend on revolver access and on delivery of management's expected return to positive free cash flow, which is a management expectation (RQ2 page:3).

- Sponsor alignment. Evidence: 950 of equity contributions and no fiscal 2027 distribution, against a new affiliate royalty. Mechanism: the parent has put in cash when the programme needed it; there is no stated obligation. Implication: treat parent support as demonstrated behavior, not a credit enhancement; the pages read contain no parent guarantee.

- Key uncertainties: timing of Bay Minette commercial shipments, the amount and timing of remaining Oswego insurance recoveries, the effect of tariffs and duties (including a customs matter in which the company carries a cash deposit of approximately 127 for antidumping duties it is appealing, Q2R page:39), a union strike at the Yeongju plant that management says may affect beverage packaging shipments (Q2R page:47), and the absence of executed financing documents.
### Consumer assessments
| Consumer | Readiness | What to take from this handoff | Why it matters | Gap and required action |

| CP-2 credit synthesis | Ready with limitations | Business model, customer concentration, parent behavior, Bay Minette and Oswego timelines, financing history | Explains why leverage and short-term borrowings rose and what must happen for deleveraging | No executed agreements or ratings; carry capacity to distribute and guarantee scope as unverified |

| CP-5 evidence trace | Ready | Every fact here has a page locator and a category tag; management estimates are tagged Management Language | Allows the trace to test claims against the filings | Check the Bay Minette timing statement and the customer concentration figures against the cited pages |
### Conflicts

One internal inconsistency is logged and not reconciled. The annual report debt table lists "Series 2026A Bonds, due June 2033" (AR page:145) while its footnote says the bonds have "a mandatory tender for purchase on March 1, 2033" (AR page:145) and the Q2 quarterly report table lists "Series 2026A Bonds, due March 2033" (Q2R page:17). The amount is 225 and the difference is one quarter in the tender date label; the financial base used the later report's maturity buckets, which do not depend on the label. Two differences of basis are noted so they are not mistaken for conflicts. Total shipments of 3,731 kt in the annual report business section include affiliates on a proportionately consolidated basis and intersegment sales (AR page:20; page:21), while the release reports rolled product shipments of 3,557 kt for the same fiscal year (RQ4 page:1); they are different measures. Segment net sales add to more than consolidated net sales for the same reason (AR page:20; AR page:21).
## Calculations

No new arithmetic was performed in this handoff. Figures repeat the financial base handoff or the cited filing pages. The one derived comparison, the Bay Minette timing, compares milestone dates stated in two documents and involves no calculation.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Consumers | Remediation |

| Executed indentures, credit agreements and bond loan agreements not supplied; capacity for distributions, additional debt and collateral release unverified | High | CP-2 | Obtain the documents, or keep all capacity statements at filing-summary level |
| No rating agency material, outlooks or market quotes | Medium | CP-2 | Leave ratings and market-implied views Not supplied |
| Control rights, shareholder agreements and any parent support commitment not stated in the pages read | Medium | CP-2 | Treat parent support as behavior only |

| Remaining Oswego insurance recoveries and the total cost are estimates; the fire cash impact of about 1.7 billion is a management estimate at the date of the annual report | Medium | CP-2 | Carry as management estimate with the cumulative recoveries of 519 as the documented figure |

| Bay Minette total cost, funded and unfunded amount at September 30, 2026 are not itemized in the pages read beyond the approximately 5.0 billion programme size | Medium | CP-2 | Use capital spending guidance; do not compute remaining cost |
| Use of proceeds for the 2026 term loan is not stated | Low | CP-2 | Leave as Insufficient Information |
| Covenant certificate and a covenant add-back bridge are not supplied; the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation is the only bridge | Medium | CP-2 | State that Adjusted EBITDA is not a covenant measure |
| Earnings slides and the 10-K/A are not supplied | Low | CP-2 | Use releases and filings |
## Next module

Run CP-2 on the financial base and this business and transaction context. It should test the deleveraging claim against the Bay Minette timeline, the capital spending guidance and the revolver availability, keep the customer concentration and Adjusted EBITDA definition risks in the credit view, treat parent support as demonstrated behavior only, and carry the missing executed agreements and ratings as limits. CP-5 follows to trace the evidence.
